name: powershell-lsp
description: Real-time PowerShell diagnostics in Claude Code: as Claude edits a .ps1/.psm1/.psd1, it runs PowerShell Editor Services + PSScriptAnalyzer over that file and surfaces syntax errors and lint fixes inline. Hover/definition/references are on the roadmap.

ps_host.title: PowerShell host executable
ps_host.description: Executable used to host PowerShell Editor Services. Use 'pwsh' (PowerShell 7+, recommended and tested) or 'powershell' (Windows PowerShell 5.1).

severityThreshold.title: Severity threshold
severityThreshold.description: Least-severe level to report: Error, Warning, Information, or Hint. 'Warning' reports Errors and Warnings only.

ruleInclude.title: Include rules (comma-separated)
ruleInclude.description: If set, report ONLY these PSScriptAnalyzer rule codes (e.g. 'PSUseApprovedVerbs,PSAvoidUsingCmdletAliases'). Empty = all.

ruleExclude.title: Exclude rules (comma-separated)
ruleExclude.description: PSScriptAnalyzer rule codes to suppress (e.g. 'PSAvoidUsingWriteHost'). Empty = none.

timeoutMs.title: Client hard cap (ms)
timeoutMs.description: Total time the PostToolUse client waits before degrading to log-only.

debounceMs.title: Debounce window (ms)
debounceMs.description: Edits landing within this window fold into one analysis pass.

keepLastN.title: Log files kept per family
keepLastN.description: SessionStart sweeps each rolling log family down to this many newest files.

idleTtlMin.title: Daemon idle TTL (minutes)
idleTtlMin.description: The daemon self-terminates after this long with no diagnostics request.

perFileCap.title: Max diagnostics per file
perFileCap.description: Cap the diagnostics reported per file; the rest collapse into an 'and N more' line. '0' = no cap.

enableStats.title: Enable telemetry/stats
enableStats.description: When 'true', append one JSONL timing line per analyzed edit to logs/stats.jsonl (rotating, ~5 MB). Observe-only: never changes diagnostics output. View with scripts/show-stats.ps1. '0'/'false'/'off' disable.

settingsPath.title: PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 path (override)
settingsPath.description: Absolute path to a PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 the analyzer should honor. Overrides auto-discovery (the nearest PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 walked up from the edited file, bounded at the project root). Must be ABSOLUTE; a relative value is ignored. Empty = auto-discover.

scopeToEdit.title: Scope diagnostics to the edited lines
scopeToEdit.description: When 'true' (default), filter the surfaced diagnostics to those overlapping the lines the edit touched (plus editContextLines of context), so the feedback is what the edit is responsible for rather than the whole file. '0'/'false'/'off' report whole-file. Fails open to whole-file whenever the touched range cannot be determined (a new-file Write, a failed edit, an unparseable payload) -- scoping never hides a diagnostic.

editContextLines.title: Edit-scope context lines
editContextLines.description: Extra lines of context above and below the touched range kept when scopeToEdit is on. The edit's structured patch already includes a few context lines, so the default is 0; raise it to widen the window.

formatOnEdit.title: Format-on-edit suggestion
formatOnEdit.description: When 'suggest', after an edit the warm daemon runs PSScriptAnalyzer's Invoke-Formatter on the edited file (honoring the repo's PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 formatter rules) and surfaces the formatted result as a SUGGESTION (a unified diff) -- it NEVER rewrites your file. 'apply' additionally WRITES the formatted result back, guarded: a stale-write compare-and-swap aborts the write if the file changed since formatting (the newer edit always wins), the write is atomic (never a torn file), the original BOM and dominant line-ending style are preserved (the only byte change is the formatting itself), and an applied write is announced loudly so you re-read before your next edit. 'off' (default) does nothing and the diagnostics surface is unchanged. Values: 'off' (default), 'suggest', 'apply'; 'apply' is doubly opt-in (only the exact value 'apply', never a boolean) and aborts to a suggestion for mixed-line-ending or non-UTF-8 files.

ruleset.title: Live diagnostics ruleset
ruleset.description: Which PSScriptAnalyzer rule set to apply on the live edit path when no repo-local PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 and no settingsPath override resolve. 'pses-default' (default) keeps PowerShell Editor Services' built-in no-settings rule set (about 15 rules) -- the surface is unchanged from prior versions. 'base' opts in to the plugin's shipped enumerated base ruleset: PSScriptAnalyzer's full default-on set minus the compatibility-profile rules, which broadens the live surface (e.g. PSAvoidUsingWriteHost and the three Error-severity security rules PSAvoidUsingComputerNameHardcoded / PSAvoidUsingConvertToSecureStringWithPlainText / PSAvoidUsingUsernameAndPasswordParams start surfacing). A repo-local PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 and an explicit settingsPath ALWAYS win over the base. Values: 'pses-default' (default), 'base'.

moduleAwareness.title: Module awareness (uninstalled-module hint)
moduleAwareness.description: When 'suggest', after an edit the warm daemon adds an Information-severity hint when a command in the edited file is exported by a KNOWN module (a shipped, offline command->module index of common first-party / Gallery modules) that is NOT installed on this machine -- so the call would fail to resolve. The message is actionable ('N is exported by module M, which is not installed; Install-Module M or import it'). It fires ONLY on positive identification: the command is a literal index hit, not a built-in, not defined or dot-sourced or #Requires/Import-Module-declared in the file, and its module is absent from a once-per-session installed-modules snapshot the daemon takes in the background (off the critical path; the check stays silent until it is ready, and on ANY ambiguity -- a dynamic include, an unresolved dot-source -- so a missing hint never becomes a wrong one). It NEVER writes your file and adds NO edit-path network or latency (the index is a shipped artifact; install-state is read once per session). 'off' (default) does nothing and the diagnostics surface is byte-for-byte unchanged. Values: 'off' (default), 'suggest'.
